paragraphs.source_en: Like children playing by the ocean who build sand-towers with constancy and then destroy them with laughter.

units.source_en: Like children playing by the ocean who build sand-towers with constancy and then destroy them with laughter.

paragraphs.source_en: But what of those to whom life is not an ocean, and man-made laws are not sand-towers,

units.source_en: But what of those to whom life is not an ocean, and man-made laws are not sand-towers,

ja.t: 々については、どうでしょう。

paragraphs.source_en: But to whom life is a rock, and the law a chisel with which they would carve it in their own likeness? What of the cripple who hates dancers?

paragraphs.source_en: What of the ox who loves his yoke and deems the elk and deer of the forest stray and vagrant things?

units.source_en: What of the ox who loves his yoke and deems the elk and deer of the forest stray and vagrant things?

ja.t: については、どうでしょう。

paragraphs.source_en: What of the old serpent who cannot shed his skin, and calls all others naked and shameless?

units.source_en: What of the old serpent who cannot shed his skin, and calls all others naked and shameless?

paragraphs.source_en: And of him who comes early to the wedding-feast, and when over-fed and tired goes his way saying that all feasts are violation and all feasters lawbreakers?

units.source_en: And of him who comes early to the wedding-feast, and when over-fed and tired goes his way saying that all feasts are violation and all feasters lawbreakers?

ja.t: については、どうでしょう。

paragraphs.source_en: What shall I say of these save that they too stand in the sunlight, but with their backs to the sun?

ja.t: えばよいのでしょう。ただ、

paragraphs.source_en: And what is it to acknowledge the laws but to stoop down and trace their shadows upon the earth?

units.source_en: And what is it to acknowledge the laws but to stoop down and trace their shadows upon the earth?

ja.t: になぞることにほかならないのではありませんか。

paragraphs.source_en: What man’s law shall bind you if you break your yoke but upon no man’s prison door?

units.source_en: What man’s law shall bind you if you break your yoke but upon no man’s prison door?

ja.t: にぶつけないなら、どんな

paragraphs.source_en: And who is he that shall bring you to judgment if you tear off your garment yet leave it in no man’s path?

units.source_en: And who is he that shall bring you to judgment if you tear off your garment yet leave it in no man’s path?

paragraphs.source_en: People of Orphalese, you can muffle the drum, and you can loosen the strings of the lyre, but who shall command the skylark not to sing?

units.source_en: People of Orphalese, you can muffle the drum, and you can loosen the strings of the lyre, but who shall command the skylark not to sing?

ja.t: をゆるめることもできます。しかし、

paragraphs.source_en: At the city gate and by your fireside I have seen you prostrate yourself and worship your own freedom,

units.source_en: At the city gate and by your fireside I have seen you prostrate yourself and worship your own freedom,

paragraphs.source_en: Even as slaves humble themselves before a tyrant and praise him though he slays them.

units.source_en: Even as slaves humble themselves before a tyrant and praise him though he slays them.

paragraphs.source_en: Ay, in the grove of the temple and in the shadow of the citadel I have seen the freest among you wear their freedom as a yoke and a handcuff.

units.source_en: Ay, in the grove of the temple and in the shadow of the citadel I have seen the freest among you wear their freedom as a yoke and a handcuff.

paragraphs.source_en: And my heart bled within me; for you can only be free when even the desire of seeking freedom becomes a harness to you, and when you cease to speak of freedom as a goal and a fulfilment.
